Class TileGUI

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.layout.Pane
javafx.scene.layout.StackPane
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.gui.PopupPane
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.gui.TileGUI
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget
public class TileGUI extends PopupPane
GUI component representing a board tile that players can place their pawn on.

Each TileGUI extends PopupPane to inherit hover scaling and the styled tooltip sourced from TileRegistry. On top of the tile image it layers:

  • A TotemGUI pawn placed via addPawn(TotemGUI) when a player occupies the tile.
  • A gold pulsing Rectangle (highlightRectangle) shown over the card slot when the tile is selectable by the current player, toggled by setHighlight(boolean).
  • An arrow indicator composed of two HBox groups (upBox for gold up-draws, downBox for light-blue down-draws), shown when the tile's draw actions are available, managed by setArrowHighlight(int, int).

Tiles without an arrow area (e.g. Tile_0) have arrowBounds, arrowIndicatorBox, upBox and downBox set to null; arrow-related methods are no-ops for those tiles.

  • Constructor Details

    • TileGUI

      public TileGUI(int tileId)
      Constructs a TileGUI for the tile with the given ID.

      Loads the tile image via TileImagesLoader, reads slot and arrow metadata from TileRegistry, and conditionally builds the arrow indicator subcomponents. All pawn and highlight layers are initialized but kept hidden until explicitly activated.

      Parameters:
      tileId - the unique identifier of the tile, used to retrieve its image, description, and layout data from the registry

  • Method Details

    • setHighlight

      public void setHighlight(boolean on)
      Activates or deactivates the gold pulsing highlight on the tile's card slot.

      Used by GameController to signal to the current player that this tile is a valid move target. When turned on, a FadeTransition is created lazily and played indefinitely. When turned off, the animation is stopped and the rectangle hidden.

      Parameters:
      on - true to show and animate the highlight; false to stop the animation and hide it

    • setArrowHighlight

      public void setArrowHighlight(int upDraws, int downDraws)
      Updates the arrow indicator to show the number of available up-draw and down-draw actions on this tile for the current player's turn.

      Up-draw slots are rendered in gold (COLOR_UP) on the right subgroup; down-draw slots in light blue (COLOR_DOWN) on the left subgroup. Each active slot pulses via a staggered FadeTransition; inactive slots remain invisible but still occupy their fixed width so that active slot positions do not shift.

      If both counts exceed the currently allocated slot count, all slots are rebuilt to accommodate the new maximum before being applied. Passing (0, 0) hides the indicator entirely.

      This method is a no-op for tiles that have no arrow area.

      Parameters:
      upDraws - the number of up-draw action slots to highlight (gold); must be ≥ 0
      downDraws - the number of down-draw action slots to highlight (light blue); must be ≥ 0

    • buildGroup

      private void buildGroup(javafx.scene.layout.HBox box, int max, javafx.scene.paint.Color color, List<javafx.animation.FadeTransition> anims)
      Populates an arrow indicator group with max fixed-size animated slots.

      Each slot is a rounded Rectangle stroked in color with a matching DropShadow glow. A FadeTransition is created per slot with a 120 ms staggered delay so that adjacent slots pulse at slightly different phases. Animations are stored in anims for later control via applyGroup(HBox, List, int, int).

      This method should be called only once per group per rebuild; call resetArrowSize() or clear the box before rebuilding.

      Parameters:
      box - the HBox to populate with slot rectangles
      max - the total number of slots to create
      color - the stroke and glow color for the slots
      anims - the list to append each slot's FadeTransition to

    • applyGroup

      private void applyGroup(javafx.scene.layout.HBox box, List<javafx.animation.FadeTransition> anims, int max, int active)
      Shows and animates the first active slots in a group, hiding the rest.

      Hidden slots use setVisible(false) rather than being removed, so they still occupy their fixed width in the layout and active slots do not shift position as the count changes.

      Parameters:
      box - the HBox containing the pre-built slot rectangles
      anims - the corresponding list of FadeTransition animations
      max - the total number of slots in the group
      active - the number of slots to make visible and animate (from index 0)

    • resetArrowSize

      public void resetArrowSize()
      Fully resets the arrow indicator slots back to the tile's baseline capacity.

      Stops and discards all running animations, then rebuilds upBox and downBox with exactly tileMaxUp and tileMaxDown slots respectively, matching the maximums defined in TileData. The indicator is hidden after the reset.

      Should be called by GameController at the start of each turn before invoking setArrowHighlight(int, int) with the new values, to ensure that any over-allocated slots from a previous turn are discarded.

    • addPawn

      public void addPawn(TotemGUI pawn)
      Places a TotemGUI pawn on this tile at the fixed pawn anchor position.

      If the pawn is currently attached to another parent container, it is detached first to avoid duplicate-parent exceptions. After placement the tile is marked as occupied.

      Parameters:
      pawn - the TotemGUI representing the player's totem to place

    • removePawn

      public void removePawn(TotemGUI pawn)
      Removes a specific TotemGUI pawn from this tile and marks it as unoccupied.
      Parameters:
      pawn - the TotemGUI to remove

    • isOccupied

      public boolean isOccupied()
      Returns whether this tile currently holds a pawn.
      Returns:
      true if a TotemGUI has been placed via addPawn(TotemGUI) and not yet removed; false otherwise

    • clearPawn

      public void clearPawn()
      Removes all pawns from this tile and marks it as unoccupied.

      Typically called during a full board reset or at the end of a round when all players' pawns are returned.
